title: New agent — the create form and the gates in front of it

data.name: strategies
data.shape: ListStrategiesResult + listings ('strategies' | 'unreadable'; readable-and-empty is its own branch)

data.name: composed
data.shape: Record<string,string> — what a refused submit carried back in the query string (problem and idempotencyKey excluded)

components.purpose: Create an agent — or say, before anything is composed, exactly why one cannot be created right now.

actions.effect: Every refusal branch links back to /agents; the strategies-empty branch links to /strategies instead

components.current_implementation: max-w-2xl centered column. Gates resolve in order before the form renders: capacity (role=status explanation, no form), catalog unreadable (role=alert naming the reason + WhyNotLoaded), strategies unreadable (role=alert, danger tokens, + WhyNotLoaded), strategies readable-and-empty (plain prose — nothing failed, there is nothing to bind to, link to /strategies). Only then the form. `?problem=` mounts CarriedProblem on EVERY branch including all four gates; bounced field values are re-read from the query (problem and idempotencyKey excluded) and passed to the form as defaults.
constraints: The gates run BEFORE the form: a user is told an agent cannot be created before composing one, never after submitting (the page's own stated requirement)

CarriedProblem mounts on every branch. A duplicate press whose first press succeeded arrives at-capacity by construction, so the branch a bounce lands on is exactly the one that must not drop it (#240's lesson)

strategies-empty is not a failure and must not be styled as one — the account is connected, nothing errored, there is nothing to bind to; it offers /strategies, deliberately not a create-strategy call to action

catalog-unreadable branches on the failure kind, never on 'not the good case' — the cause distinguishes a refusal (fix the credential) from an outage (waiting is right), and collapsing them once sent users to wait for an outage that was not happening

components.purpose: Compose the agent: name, the strategy it reads, its brain, position management, and the six money answers.

actions.effect: Submits the create server action. Success redirects to /agents/<id>. A refusal bounces back here as ?problem= with every typed field riding along. A duplicate press bounces with a sentence naming what the first press did (succeeded, or not yet recorded), and the composition deliberately does not ride that bounce

components.current_implementation: Native form posting to the create action. Name (text, required, maxLength 80), strategy select (required, nothing preselected; each option names the strategy, its scope as 'BattleGrid' or 'Yours', and its revision), Brain fieldset (preset select OR model select + three behavior enums — the union is decided server-side from which control was used; when the platform declares no presets, a role=status sentence says so and only the model route renders), Position management fieldset (CUSTOM first and default; only presets whose full config arrived are offered), MoneyLimits, PerformButton ('Creating the agent…'). A hidden idempotencyKey input, minted per render by the page.
constraints: The strategy is NEVER preselected. The platform materializes the strategy onto the agent — it is how the agent will reason about the operator's money, and choosing one on their behalf binds funds to a policy nobody read

The hidden idempotencyKey is minted per render and carried through the form — this is the entire dedupe mechanism (a double press, a back-button replay, a second tab all resend the key they were rendered with). A design must not remove it, regenerate it client-side, or move minting into the action
Scope rides on each strategy option ('BattleGrid' / 'Yours') — it decides whether the strategy can later be edited or only forked, and must not be dropped for visual economy
An empty preset list renders the role=status sentence, never an empty select — the declaration not answering and BattleGrid having no presets are different facts
Position management offers only presets whose twelve-field config actually arrived — a label with no values behind it is the old wired-to-nothing defect wearing a new control

Every state change is a full navigation and the form holds no client state; the only client code is PerformButton ('use client', useFormStatus), which reports that a submit is in flight and nothing else

components.purpose: The six questions BattleGrid will not answer for anybody: trading mode and the five money caps.
components.current_implementation: Consequence-tinted fieldset shared verbatim with the edit surface. Trading mode select with OFF first and default; five required number inputs in a 2-col grid (1-col mobile), each with a label, an aria-describedby hint, and — on the three fields BattleGrid reads 0 as no-cap — a bold 'Entering 0 removes this limit' warning beside the box. On the create form the boxes start empty (no number chosen on the operator's behalf); a bounce refills them from what was typed. An APPROVAL_REQUIRED note states plainly that answering approvals is not possible in this product yet.
constraints: OFF stays first and default — it is the only answer that makes the other five harmless, and this ordering is the difference between creating something that reasons and something that spends
The zero-removes-this-limit warning renders beside the box it is typed into, not in a paragraph above the form
The fields are derived from undefaultableFields(catalog), never enumerated — if BattleGrid starts defaulting one it stops being asked, without anyone editing this file
One component serves create and edit; the zero-means-unbounded wording must not fork between the screen that creates an agent and the screen that changes it
No money box may carry a suggested value on a first visit — a pre-filled loss cap is this product choosing a number on the operator's behalf

components.purpose: Keep the reason a bounced write carried back visible, whichever branch renders next.
components.current_implementation: Shared component; renders nothing without a problem, otherwise a role=alert danger-tinted paragraph with the bold 'Refused: ' prefix (DT-0004's ruling — named as well as tinted).
constraints: Every branch mounts it unconditionally — rendering nothing when there is no problem is the mechanism that makes that safe, and it must stay
The 'Refused:' prefix is load-bearing: a refusal must be named as well as tinted

components.purpose: Tell a user their work still exists, and say accurately why it could not be shown.
components.current_implementation: The shared sentence, rendered under both unreadable gates with subjects 'BattleGrid's catalogue is' and 'your strategies are'.
constraints: refused and unreachable must not be collapsed — naming the wrong one sends a user to wait for an outage that is not happening
The cause arrives as a value on the result; nothing here may re-derive it from the reason text

components.purpose: Turn away a request with no authority.
components.current_implementation: Shared component rendered in place of the page body. Reachable only on a delegated deployment.
constraints: One page for every cause; they differ in cause and not in remedy (design W-C)

flows.name: Create an agent
steps: pass the four gates (capacity, catalog, strategies readable, strategies non-empty)
compose: name, strategy, brain, position preset, six money answers

flows.name: A refused create keeps what was typed
steps: refusal bounces to /agents/new?problem= with fields riding along
CarriedProblem names the refusal; every control re-fills from the bounce
fix the named field, submit again with a fresh idempotency key

focus_order: brain preset or model + behavior enums
accessibility.notes: Labels are htmlFor-bound; money hints are aria-describedby. Carried problems and the two unreadable gates are role=alert; capacity and the no-presets sentence are role=status. Money boxes use inputMode=decimal.
